issue.title: Deck-state save can clobber fixed deck views when a TUI dies abruptly or a second TUI saves last
issue.description:
Proposed by sase-1b1.8.3 (live deck-views drive, 2026-09-27). While killing `sase screenshot` TUI windows with `tmux kill-window`, `~/.sase/ace_agents_deck_state.json` reverted to auto/single, losing a fixed `spread` view set with `P`. Single-window P-save, graceful `q` quit preservation, and fresh-launch restore were all verified working, so the suspect is the save path under abrupt teardown or two concurrent TUIs: a dying TUI (or a second concurrent one) writes transitional/empty deck state last, and last-writer-wins clobbers the user's fixed views.

Repro sketch: start two `sase tui` sessions (or one and kill it via tmux kill-window mid-teardown); in one, press `P` on a Main deck to fix a view; kill the other; inspect ace_agents_deck_state.json.

Location: deck-state persistence (`src/sase/ace/tui/models/agent_deck_persistence.py` save path and its callers on unmount/teardown). Remediation to consider: skip saves during teardown when the deck area is not fully mounted, and/or merge-or-guard concurrent writers.

task_type_fields.impact: Users silently lose fixed deck views and split layout across restarts.
task_type_fields.repro: Two sase tui sessions (or tmux kill-window during teardown); press P in one to fix a Main view; kill the other; ace_agents_deck_state.json reverts to auto/single.

issue.creation_reason: The sase-1b1.8.3 live drive saw persisted fixed views revert to auto after tmux kill-window; it is outside the deck-views landing scope.
